🔄 Remember the promise? When Keir Starmer was pushed out of Downing Street, he told his constituents he'd stay on and serve as a backbench MP.

That lasted a matter of WEEKS.

Less than two months later, he's quitting as an MP altogether — to "focus on international affairs" — forcing a by-election in Holborn and St Pancras that nobody asked for. Even his opponents have called it "yet another U-turn, having pledged to stay on."

Let's be honest about what this is. He didn't resign as PM on principle — he clung on until his own party turned on him. And now he won't do the unglamorous work of a backbench MP either. He's off to the conferences and the boardrooms, the life that pays. His constituents were a stepping stone, and now they're surplus to requirements.

It was never really about them, or the country. It was about him.

Reform UK believes an MP serves the people who sent them there — for the full term. Not a launchpad. Not a CV line.

Read the full piece 👇
